persona.role: The lane's queue matriarch, in her sixties; she keeps order at the standpipe and remembers whose turn it is.
persona.voice: Loud enough to run a queue, kind enough to remember a sick neighbour's bucket.
persona.wants: Every household filled before the lock shuts.
taboos: Never lets anyone hold a place for money
Never wastes a drop of water, not even to wash her own hands
Never repeats what she hears at the pipe

lore: Aunt Mak has run the standpipe queue since the rationing began: a few hours every few days, buckets named in chalk, her voice for a bell. She trades a bucket for news without ever calling it a debt. She has watched the lane's children grow up counting turns instead of sheep.

secrets.text: The pipe opens a few hours every few days; she carries the schedule by heart and plans every household's cooking around it.
In the black album she recognizes the lane before the new lock — when the water ran all day and nobody had to be told whose turn it was.

greeting.en: Did you bring a bucket? No bucket, no queue.

lines.zh_HK: 制水制水，幾日先嚟一次水。個鐘一開，全巷企滿人。
lines.zh_CN: 制水制水，几天才来一次水。龙头一开，全巷站满人。
lines.en: Rationing — a few days between supplies. The moment the lock turns, the lane fills up.

lines.zh_HK: 水要煮滾先飲得，洗完衫嘅水仲要沖地。一滴都係時間。
lines.zh_CN: 水要烧滚才能喝，洗完衣服的水还要冲地。一滴都是时间。
lines.en: Water must be boiled before drinking, and washing water does the floor after. Every drop is somebody's time.

text.zh_HK: 你企得乖。攞住呢個銅喉嘴——排隊嗰陣唔怕人爭。
text.zh_CN: 你站得守规矩。拿着这个铜水管嘴——排队的时候不怕人抢。
text.en: You queue politely. Take this brass tap cap — with it, no one can jump your turn.
